title: Monotonicity of the decision-tree depth tail under Bernoulli restrictions
statement:
Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean function, let $t \in \bbn$ be a threshold, and let $p_1, p_2 \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p_1 \le 1$ and $0 < p_2 \le 1$. For a parameter $p$, let $\Pr_p[\,\cdot\,]$ denote the probability of an event under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$, in which each variable is left free with probability $p$ and is otherwise fixed to a constant Boolean value, each of the two values with probability $(1-p)/2$. For a restriction $\rho$, write $f_\rho$ for the function of the free coordinates obtained from $f$ by fixing each set coordinate $i$ to the value $\rho(i)$, and let $D(f_\rho)$ be its decision-tree depth, that is, the least $d$ for which some decision tree of depth at most $d$ computes $f_\rho$. Then
\[
  \Pr_{p_1 p_2}\bigl[D(f_\rho) > t\bigr] \le
  \Pr_{p_1}\bigl[D(f_\rho) > t\bigr].
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on Fin n → Bool
replaced:
For every Boolean function $f$, threshold $t$, and parameters $p_1, p_2 \in (0,1]$, the
probability that the restricted depth exceeds $t$ under the stronger Bernoulli restriction
of parameter $p_1 p_2$ is at most that under parameter $p_1$:
\[
  \Pr_{p_1 p_2}\bigl[\mathrm{dtDepth}(f|_\rho) > t\bigr] \le
  \Pr_{p_1}\bigl[\mathrm{dtDepth}(f|_\rho) > t\bigr].
\]
